text:
A. Phenyl methanamine

B. N,N-Dimethylaniline

C. N-Methyl aniline

D. Benzenamine

Choose the correct order of basic nature of the above amines.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In phenyl methanamine, the lone pair on nitrogen of $-NH_{2}$
group is localised and does not undergo resonance.


[IMG]


(B), (C) and (D) are aromatic amines in which lone pair of electrons
of N-atoms goes in resonance
(+R effect) with the benzene ring. So, Lewis basicity or donation of
lone pair of electrons of these amines will be decreased in comparison to
(A).


[IMG]


+ I effects of two $-CH_{3}$
groups increases electron density on N atom while lone pair of N atom take part in resonance with the benzene ring and decreases electron density on N atom. Both this effect try to compensate each other.


[IMG]


+ I effects of one $-CH_{3}$
groups increases electron density on N atom while lone pair of N atom take part in resonance with the benzene ring and decreases electron density on N atom. Both this effect try to compensate each other.


[IMG]


It has no + I-effect on N-atom to increase electron density on the N atom which was decreased due to lone pair of N atom take part in resonance with the benzene ring.
So, A is purely aliphatic 1°-amine. B is aromatic.
3°-amine with more aliphatic nature (for two $-CH_{3}$
groups). C is
aromatic 2°-amine with less aliphatic nature (for one $-CH_{3}$
group).

D is purely aromatic 1°-amine.

Hence basicity order is A > B > C > D.

text: The correct order of electron gain enthalpy is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Oxygen is the second most electronegative element in comparison to fluorine. In group - 16 family $(\mathrm{O},\mathrm{S},\mathrm{Se},\mathrm{Te})$, O-atom is smallest in size. So, electron density on O-atom is very high in group -16
During addition of a free electron to gaseous $\mathrm{O}$-atom,

$\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{e}^{-}⟶\mathrm{O}^{-}(\mathrm{g})$

We have to supply a significant amount of energy (endothermic) to overcome the electrostatic repulsion between the approaching electron and O-atom of very high electron density. So, the net value of electron affinity (EA) or (negative) electron gain enthalpy $[\Delta _{\mathrm{eg}}H$ or $|\Delta _{\mathrm{eg}}H|]$ of oxygen decreases to a higher extent in comparison to other elements of group -16 who have larger size and lower electronegativity.

So, the correct order of EA or $|\Delta _{\mathrm{eg}}\mathrm{H}|$ of group $-16$ elements will be $\mathrm{S}$ $>\mathrm{Se}>\mathrm{Te}>\mathrm{O}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift

text: When 12.2 g of benzoic acid is dissolved in 100 g of water, the freezing point of solution was found to be $-$0.93${}^{\circ }C (K_{f}(H_{2}O) = 1.86 K kg$ mol$^{-1})$. The number (n) of benzoic acid molecules associated (assuming 100% association) is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$n\mathrm{PhCOOH}_{\text{Benzoic acid}}⟶^{\text{Association}}(\mathrm{PhCOOH})_{n}$

Assuming $100%$ association ( $α=1$ ),

$\Rightarrow i=1-α\left (1-\frac{1}{n}\right )=\frac{1}{n}[\because α=1]$

Now, $\Delta T_{f}=K_{f}\times m\times i$

$0-(-0.93)=1.86\times \frac{w_{B}\times 1000}{w_{A}\times M_{B}}\times \frac{1}{n}$

$[\because w_{B}=$ mass of $\mathrm{PhCOOH}=12.2\mathrm{g}$

$w_{A}=$ mass of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}=100\mathrm{g}$

$M_{B}=$ molar mass of $\mathrm{PhCOOH}]$

$=122\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

$=1.86\times \frac{12.2\times 1000}{100\times 122}\times \frac{1}{n}$

$\begin{array}{ll} \Rightarrow n & =\dfrac{1.86\times 12.2\times 1000}{0.93\times 100\times 122}=2 \end{array}$

$\therefore$ Number of benzoic acid molecules associated, $n=2$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift

text:
A ball weighing 10 g is moving with a velocity of $90 ms^{-1}$. If the uncertainty in its velocity is 5%, then the uncertainty in its position is $___________$ $\times$ $10^{-33} m. ($Rounded off to the nearest integer)

[Given : h = 6.63 $\times$ $10^{-34} Js$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$m = 10 g = 10^{-2} Kg$

v = 90 m/sec.

$\Delta$v = v $\times$ 5% = 90 $\times$ $\frac{5}{100}$ = 4.5 m/sec

m . $\Delta$v . $\Delta$x $\geq$ $\frac{h}{4π}$

$10^{-2}$ $\times$ 4.5 $\times$ $\Delta$x $\geq$ $\frac{6.63\times 10^{-34}}{4\times \frac{22}{7}}$

$\Delta$x $\geq$ $\frac{6.63\times 7\times 2\times 10^{-34}}{9\times 4\times 22\times 10^{-2}}$

$\Delta$x $\geq$ 1.17 $\times$ $10^{-33} = x$ $\times$ $10^{-33}$

x = 1.17 $\simeq$ 1
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift
